seoChanges.old: Google Cloud says its new Gemini agent runs business tasks for hours or days. A 656-case study finds AI agents often act before checking the facts.
seoChanges.new: Google Cloud says its Gemini agent works for hours or days and gives coworker agents their own email. A preprint finds AI agents often act before checking.
seoChanges.reason: Launch coverage that now ranks for this topic (Decrypt, Developers Digest, TechRepublic and others) leads with 'coworker agents with their own email', which the old description left out. The new text also labels the study a preprint, as the style guide requires. It keeps the 'says' and 'often' hedges and is 155 characters. Title left as is: 'Gemini agent for work' still matches how people phrase searches.

Gemini agent: Google's Cloud blog and the Google Blog post have no editor's notes or updates, and the quotes and figures in the issue still match (roster of sub-agents, hours or days, Claude models today, audit trail, 80%/90%). TechCrunch and Computerworld show no corrections, and their attributed details still match. I could not find that in Google's own posts, so I added nothing.
